utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Dr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I wonder if I could clarify very briefly one matter arising out of the admission of associated exhibits. As Your Honours will recall, yesterday you decided not to admit reports dealing with nonscheduled incidents. Now, on page 33 of the witness's statement, he does refer to two incidents, and each of those incidents concerns an impact which took place at approximately the same time as the Markale 2 impact and each of the shells bears the same markings on the stabiliser to indicate that they were -- the stabilisers were manufactured in Krusik in Valjevo, in Serbia, in July of 1993. So I would tender those two reports in order for Your Honours to have to rely upon, if Your Honours wish, as being an integral part of the evidence concerning the question of who fired the Markale 2 projectile, for that specific purpose. So for that reason, I tender both of those reports which -- both of which fall under the 65 ter number 16835.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me be clear. This relates to another shell in Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: They relate to -- to -- a series of shells were fired on that morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: These are two of the shells which dropped not at Markale 2 but in the centre of Sarajevo. So they form part of the same series of shells. So the paragraph number 18 and paragraph number 19 are two of that series of shells. They were nonfatal, I understand. Markale 2 was the only projectile that resulted in fatalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But he states in his statement that all those are -- shells were manufactured in Krusik Valjevo in July 1993? So that's in evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I appreciate that point very much, but in order for Your Honours to have the actual reports at your disposal, I would tender the reports too, just to give Your Honours the option of relying on the reports themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are of the view that the statements would suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will have to make pauses between question and answer to enable interpreters to do their job. While we're at it, Mr. Turkusic, if somebody wanted to trick you experts by believing that a mine was produced -- a shell was produced in Serbia in 1993, that would not be a big problem, would it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. The question is inviting speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not for the witness to answer, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe the witness told us that 4 per cent of shells do not explode, that those shells cannot have anything other useful than explosives. Nothing but explosive explodes, and everything else remains, and these remains can deceitfully represented as something produced in Serbia, the remains of the shell that did not explode.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that a question? Can you make a comment on that statement, Dr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, I can comment. The stabiliser of any shell that exploded and a shell that did explode would be the same in terms of your speculation that something was passed off as something else, but I, as a witness of the truth, cannot follow that argument which is hypothetical. I am only testifying about facts that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to confirm that they did pass something off for something else. I'm just asking, did they have stabilisers of shells produced in Krusik Valjevo in Serbia? Did your army have such stabilisers?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're confusing stabilisers and shells themselves. A shell that did not explode cannot be launched again, cannot be used again for an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can a tail fin be placed somewhere, just be placed on an incident site without trying to explode anything?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that because you're asking me to follow your train of speculation, so to speak. You know that hypothetically any one of us can do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's enough. Thank you. You investigated the incident in the queue for water. It used to be the school called Simon Bulevar. Now it's called Skender Kulenovic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you conclude there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I simply want to point out that this incident has been dropped from the indictment. We are not leading any evidence. I'm not suggesting that cross-examination needs to be stopped. I'm just making Your Honours aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You're moving to another incident, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to use this example to show the pattern of inaccurate conclusions of which my indictment is full, as well as the indictments against other Serbs. This is a howling example of how that is done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, but could you do that very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by the conclusion that was submitted to the Prosecutor's office, the final conclusion about the direction of fire in the case of this shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember the case correctly, that shell hit the frame of the window of the gym, the very edge, and spilling shrapnel downwards, killed a large number of people who were wounded in the upper parts of the body from up high. That was near the water pump. If that's what you mean, I stand by definitely -- by the azimuth we determined, and I remember that investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then I don't need to call the report, or should I?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can call our report if you're going to ask about details from it, but I know that -- I'm trying to select the right word for a report of a foreign military investigator which shows a very wrong direction in a very wrong way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then I will have to call the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I get 65 ter 15053.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's the calibre of that shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you give me the source document, please? It could be, if I remember well, 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the right document. 65 ter 15053, official report. ERN 0033-4859. Page 5 in this number. If this is 15053, then it is page 5. The ERN number is 0033-4859. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the first page, and your name is under number 5 here; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Probably on the next page here there is a conclusion that a 120-millimetre shell hit there.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you show me that next page? I have to refresh my memory. This was 15 years ago, after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the English translation as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the right document in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English is another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the last but one line in the second column in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only see Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay. Call it whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wrote in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's my treat.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need your treats. Just call it whatever it's called. Which line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last but one line of paragraph 2. Below the place where the shell hit the wall, calibre, 120 millimetres. A number of shrapnel was found originating from the exploded projectile.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is that line? I believe this tail fin and the rest of the material was collected by members of the CSB, the security services centre. And I believe in the file, on page 1, we can see their names and affiliation. It would be good to see the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will. Do you confirm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to see the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "Traces of mechanical -- of machining --" it's the second paragraph in English.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says 120-millimetre mortar shell, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that shell hit the wall three or four metres high from the side of the atrium where a water pump was mounted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which part of the job did you do here?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first job here was to determine the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you made a sketch.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the sketch and an analysis of the scene, and the photographs later, of course, but the scene itself gives much more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You determined north, north-west, which corresponds to the aggressor barracks in Nedzarici. Did you also determine the station -- sorry, the distance?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With the distance you have the same problem with every shell. You have to know the angle and the charge. It's common knowledge, nothing new.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement of 24 November 1994: "I'm making a sketch on the scene. First of all, I used the method of elimination. I marked on the drawing directions that have been ruled out as impossible under numbers 1, 2, and 3," and a negative sign in a circle. Did you use indeed the method of elimination?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to show me that picture with numbers 1, 2, and 3. And mentioning this methodology, elimination results from the fact that on our television that night in the news bulletin, it was said that the shell had come from an easterly direction, which relative to this site would be Lukavica barracks. However, if you look at the impact and the site, it was practically impossible. Not even a guided missile Maljutka could do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 65 ter 09969, page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "I'm making a drawing of the situation on site."

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you marked it, and you say: "We also take into account the traces numbered 6. They are traces we take in consideration to determine the direction of fire. These are traces caused by shrapnel." That's also useful when determining the direction of fire; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D02191.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this map can you mark primary school Skender -- sorry, Simon Bulevar, later called Skender Kulenovic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it's probably the red rectangle. It's slightly deeper inside relative to this street that cuts through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you extend the east wall with a line both upwards and downwards?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The east wall of the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If that's the school.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's the school. I'm not a cartographer, nor can I immediately recognise what you have been studying for a long time probably. This is the school, and the map is or -- if the map is oriented north-south, then this red rectangle would probably be the school. Inside it is an atrium, and the east wall would be this. I will extend that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that would be the west wall. You can extend both lines, but if you agree, the east wall is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we erase this and try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the east wall is between the red rectangle and the letter Sh?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm asking this question for myself: Suppose, hypothetically, you may succeed in raising a reasonable doubt as to this incident. It was removed from the indictment. The Prosecution did not rely on this. What could -- could your success assist your defence at all? I'm at a loss. Why are you delving into such detail about this incident? Be brief. Just put your case and get the answer from the witness. I don't see any point of going into such detail with this removed incident.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the model on which they determine the direction of fire is identical. In many cases, this witness did that job or other people on his team, in his service, and everywhere they did the same thing. They turned the globe around. The cardinal points were moved, and then it turns out -- or it's made out to be from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the east wall and mark the direction where Dobrinja is. And very soon we will get to that.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the school, then the atrium is in the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I asked you to put your case. Put your case to the witness in relation to this and move on quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, you erroneously established on the site the disposition of the traces and shrapnel. Number two, you mis-determined the sides of the world.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Show me the photograph of the school -- of the atrium and precisely of the wall where the shell hit. It's out of the question that we determined the sides of the world erroneously or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please, then, draw an extension of the eastern wall upwards and downwards.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to play games with maps. Can I have Dobrinja from a different angle, and can I have somebody tell me if north is up on this map -- or, rather, can you enlarge the map for me to see the airport runway?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't you see the runway?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can see the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can't you see the runway at the bottom of the map?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the white shape here? If the runway is the white line going out of the map, then this is the southern side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we see the meridians on the map?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the map has the right bearing north/south, then these are the meridians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now extend the eastern wall of the school?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The eastern external wall of school would be thus disposed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D2244. Let's skip this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please place your signature and the date on the map?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, is that proper? I was asked to mark a wall, and I have no idea as to what the purpose of this will be, and is this consistent with cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. If the questions are irrelevant, we will stop the accused. You marked the location of the school for the Chamber. Could you put the date and your signature on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the wall -- the extension of the wall would go on to the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What road was it that you referred to, Mr. Karadzic? The interpreters couldn't hear that. Boulevard something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mimar Sinana, which is the street south of the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll keep it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D877, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have just for a short while 1D2244.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the school, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this Bulevar Mimar Sinana, the street from which the photograph is taken?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the white side of the school the gym?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm that the gym runs at a 90-degree angle to Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At perpendicularly?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The photograph was taken from quite the opposite street, not the one from which we would enter the school, and normally one would enter the school from the northern side. You would reach the atrium and then to your left you would have the gym. So this is the opposite view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, you would enter the school from the opposite side and you had the gym to your left?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So is this consistent with what we see on this photograph? If you enter the school from this side, the gym would be to your right. Isn't this the gym, then?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark for us where the incident took place with an arrow.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this photograph, it can only be shown as an approximation. So vertically into the atrium, and that would roughly be consistent with these two arrows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the gym so that we can tell exactly the gym from the school.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the date and signature, please.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D878.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 1 -- or, rather, 21662, page 17. Page 17. Page 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The street is now called Mustafe Kamerica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you check the 65 ter number. I checked it. It's only of two pages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have 65 ter 21662. It's a shelling documentation containing a diagram made by Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the next page, the second page. Are you referring to this one?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can have this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, did you mark here the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Nedzarici, but you cannot claim that it was fired from Nedzarici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all the trials before this Tribunal it is common knowledge that the place from where a shell was fired can be determined by the angle of descent and by knowing the charge, but -- so that we have several parameters that determine the place. The direction of fire shown here is consistent with a 360-degree angle of the azimuth. We have the bearings north-south as they should normally be. So this is consistent with the way we entered the building. To the left we have the gym and the eastern wall of the gym which was hit by the shell coming from the opposite side but at an angle shown by the azimuth, and the pattern left by the explosion can clearly be seen on the wall. We will see it in a photo later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have your diagram, which is 10357, page 6.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So 65 ter 10357, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your diagram? Or sketch.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I ask that it be confirmed that this is indeed my sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You marked here the directions of shrapnel fragments.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. I want somebody to confirm for me that this is the sketch that I made, because I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is part of that investigation report. Would you like to see the legend as well? I think it's on the previous page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you show the witness the first page of this document. No, no, not this one, the -- 15053, the report that we've seen before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the preamble.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With me it's 10357. That's the number I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this the one? There are various versions. Can you try 15053?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. There is a front page which is the 14th page of 15053, as Your Honour has said. I don't see the witness's signature on that page, I must say, but we can show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I saw previously was the cover page of the entire report. As far as I remember, the entire report was produced by the CSB Sarajevo, whereas we did what was shown in the previous slide or picture and shown in a legend which was the place where the shell landed. That was the arrow. And the azimuth below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And let's show page 11 of that previous document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document we can see the heading which indicates that it was the Security Services Centre Sarajevo which produced it, Public Security Station Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll show you everything. Page 11. From there move on to page 15 and 16. Next page. Next page. Next page. Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Previous page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Previous page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who signed this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- you can take a look again and let's move on. Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I recognise -- what I can tell, that is, is that I don't recognise the two signatures at the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment, please. I am almost certain that this sketch of the disposition of the shrapnel, places where the wounded were, is not something that I drew. And the place of the impact. If the arrow on the left marks or indicates north, I don't see that the place of impact has been shown explicitly. What would this arrow marked S stand for on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, who determined the azimuth in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did with my colleagues from the KDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said first that it was you this morning. Is this north as you marked it here?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're telling me you again. I told you that I am almost positive that I didn't draw the sketch, and I am puzzled by the arrow marked S, because it seems to indicate north. But is that north really? Had I drawn the sketch myself, I would have recognised this particular symbol and would have been sure of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are dealing, Mr. Turkusic, with an entire investigation process where you were the one determining the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to me determining the azimuth, I urge you to show me the physical evidence, which is the photograph of the impact, where I will be able to explain to you where the shell came from, hitting the walls of the gym -- the wall of the gym, and the disposition of the shrapnel as well as the general geographic direction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page. 871 is what I wanted. We seem to have a page missing here. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this something you made? You say, "I made a sketch of the scene." Is this the sketch of the scene you made?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise it. Can we have a photograph and -- that will help me tell if I made it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where in this case is the sketch you made?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't been able to see the entire case file. Can you show me all the pages and specifically the photograph of the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will come to the photograph in due time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the Prosecution to provide us with the sketch relevant in this case and the entire case file for -- in hard copy for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That would be the best if I could get a hard copy of the case file with all the pages involved so that I could find the sketch that I drew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've been down this road before. Mr. Karadzic should have hard copies ready during his cross-examination. Once again we are still on the incident which has been expressly removed from the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I do -- I do have a hard copy here with some red words written by myself on the front. I'm happy to give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you are happy with it, we will allow the witness to take a look at it. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm not representing that that's the entire case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we place on the screen another sketch that will explain this indication of north. 1D2234.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think the witness was given an opportunity by the Presiding Judge to look at the file. Perhaps he can be given a moment to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to make any correction to the statement you've made, Dr. Turkusic, after having taken a look at the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw just a part of the document. In the conclusion of this document where I can recognise my signature, we say: "Attached to this document a card -- a map with azimuth drawn in." Now, the document we saw previously on the screen is the cover page for the remaining part, then a sketch on which I confirmed -- a sketch of the neighbourhood where I confirmed the azimuth. It's also an attachment to the report. The drawing of the scene was made by people from the CSB, and then come the two sketches that I did not recognise because I did not make them, and I did not see them before. Let's move on. These are findings from the specialist of the general hospital Dobrinja. Death certificates, death certificates. I apologise to those people, the last traces of whose death I'm just leafing through like this. Statements taken from citizens gathered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, protocol of a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now that we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I really insist on being shown a photograph that unequivocally shows the azimuth and where can be no talk about the cardinal points being turned around and confusing the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to photographs, but the problem is that they were taken indoors and you cannot see any orientation or cardinal points. We see in the documentation that in this case you decided it was north.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not real north. North is an azimuth of almost 360. Anything less than 360 takes the azimuth further west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the azimuth. I'm talking about north.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D2234.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Mr. Karadzic, the compass, wherever you take it, shows the sides of the world. If we had a compass on this table, it would still be showing north, south, and east, west. The scene with clear traces just after the -- just after the explosion, the soot on the walls and the traces of TNT, all these are indubitable marks that show unequivocally the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then can you orient this and then draw -- you draw -- you drew in the -- the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is better. Here you can see the north. You can see how the school is oriented, and you can see the azimuth showing the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this case file be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The sketch at the bottom with marking, which is made, apparently, by the Defence is something you can confirm that is done correctly based upon the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood correctly, this lower drawing was made by the Defence. Of course, that makes me wary. Perhaps this is accurately done, but that makes me doubt things again, and I want things to be analysed step-by-step. Why are they avoiding to show me the photograph of the scene? It shows everything very clearly. But considering the shadows of the shrapnel, some mistakes may have been made in orientation, but they could not have changed the sides of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this visualisation of your finding correct? Is this the direction towards Nedzarici, and is this north, and is this the place of impact? The place of impact is up. We just drew in angles.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm. I have the right to be suspicious because you just said we moved the cardinal points around. That makes me suspicious, and I want us to discuss this from scratch. Let's start from the place of impact.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, Excellencies, we have to go step-by-step because this is a perfect example how this was done, and we are now in a position to disqualify, discredit all their work on just one example. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As I said earlier, let's suppose that this is done incorrectly. What impact at all does it have on another investigations? Why don't you deal with that investigation yourself? This is purely a waste of time. And more than that, the witness said that he cannot confirm this -- he cannot recognise this sketch, and he cannot confirm that the direction of north was drawn correctly or not. But what's the point of delving into such detail on this document? But having heard the witness that this was done by the CSB at the time and the sketch -- and with the caveat that the sketch on the bottom part was done by the Defence, we can admitted this. We give the Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D879, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You will have ten minutes before the break, after which you will have half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Will you please just allow me one minute. I accepted your suggestion to go through this case file skipping steps. The witness wants to go through all the steps one by one. I wanted to do what you said, just to show that everything was incorrectly determined. First of all, the disposition of fragments and then the direction. Two errors. And that's a pattern how this security services centre worked. Now, I'm putting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, there was not a single deliberate shelling of civilian areas by the Serbian side. All the incidents of massive casualties among civilians were caused by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this is proof how you laid it at the door of the Serbs. I'm going to use your case to show it.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that you said is absolutely unacceptable. I'm absolutely not going to sign this drawing of yours, because on one example you want to win this whole dispute. You want to show that a million and 500.000 shells fell on Sarajevo just by shooting at military targets. Then Sarajevo must have been targeted more than the NATO alliance. If Sarajevo had that many military targets, Sarajevo would be stronger than the whole NATO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We're not asking you to sign this document. Just please answer the question. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D2157. Page 20. And ERN is 875.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which of these photographs do you wish, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding this case, I had much better, much clearer photographs. You must have something better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is from the file.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many more photographs in this file. These are the least clear ones. However, you can recognise the main elements both on the upper side and the lower side. You can recognise the main elements of the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just let's clarify one thing. This is a complete case file that goes before the Court. This is completed material. Is this the side of the wall facing the room where the water pump is?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we should now see another photograph, 1D2209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. First of all, I want to note that this file is a duplicate of the document with 65 ter 15053, and there's an English translation under that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what page is it? I couldn't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic said 1D2157, but what we are seeing is 15053, so that's why I was wondering.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I understand. I understand the point. In any event, there is an English translation available under this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But in that case, under that number there are no photographs. And believe us, the Defence team is not making duplicates. We have only what was disclosed by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I remember very clearly that there were great photographs of this scene with recognisable traces of shrapnel and clear traces of explosion leaving black stains. You can see very unclear stains on this picture, but this is really very bad. In the archive there are very high-quality photographs. I remember them very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say that number 2 and the arrow indicate the place on the wall where the projectile impacted and exploded?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile hit and exploded where this arrow shows. If you want me to show the direction --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No need. This is the room where the water pump is.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the wall looked like, if I remember well. This corresponds to the photograph of that place. The damage to the wall, on the edge of the wall, shows the place where the shell hit and exploded. To the left and right are stains of TNT, unreactive carbon. In that direction the blast is strongest, and the shrapnel goes. The place of impact, as we see it, shows the direction of descent of the shell, although this is two dimensional. In 3D, on the scene, we used high-quality military compasses and they show north-north-west, the direction of Nedzarici. There's no question of turning or moving around the cardinal points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the shell hit from the room where the water pump is or from the gym?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither. The shell arrived from the air. That space up was completely open. Coming from the air it hit the edge of this wall, so close to the edge that the tail fin passed through into the gym that is behind the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you measure the distance between the centre of impact and this little post, this --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is that, the little one next to the wall?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the -- a bit of the frame of the window that used to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put the date and signature there, please.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I haven't got the answer. What page is this from, that 1D2157 or 15053 in e-court? In the meantime we'll keep this. We'll admit this as Exhibit D880.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1 -- 2157 is page 20. Now I'd like 1D2209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 20. Did you say page 20?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That was my question nobody answered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2209.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the same wall but viewed from the gym?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. However, I don't understand again why these photographs are so low quality. I was looking at very clear, good quality photographs on which you can see everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we show him page 21 of this previous document. It's from the case file, Dr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be fine if that's the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The doctor wanted to see other photos. Why don't you show him all and we just skip through and then show this. We start from page 19. We'll just skim through. Next page, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lower on the picture is the water pump, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this is what we saw already. Next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. We saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The photo was the one shown to you previously.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't know why this is so low quality but -- and you'd like to see the other photos as well or you are ready to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am ready to view them all. Have I seen them all? Stop. Very good. This is the tail fin that passed through, because the shell hit the very edge of the window and tail fin, with the acceleration given it by the vacuum of the centre of explosion, got additional acceleration and flew into the next room. That's where we photographed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just answer the question to be put by the accused, but now just take a look. Page 22. And from the next page there are photos of victims. I don't think you need to see them all. So go back to page 21 and zoom in the first photo. And your question, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this point of impact be zoomed in as far as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the text, at the caption below the photograph first.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small arrow indicates the point of impact, and the larger arrow indicates the place in the room where a fragment of the projectile, tail fin, was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which after impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After impact flew into the other room, and that's what I said. Into the adjacent room from the one where -- adjacent to the one where the individuals who were hurt were found by the water pump. I said so. Can we have the other photograph where there was a large stain on the wall, and can we zoom in on it as far as possible. More, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which side did the shell arrive from?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the opposite side but by the very edge of the wall, and because of the strength of the impact, the plaster or whatever the material here is was damaged. But I don't see what this -- what this white stain here is. Has it been added or was it there before?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me state for the record that the Defence made no interventions into the photograph.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean to say that, but I find the photograph unclear. Let me note that there are no black stains. It is a known fact that a TNT explosive, wherever it is, regardless of the charge where it was, whether it was the mortar or the rifle-launched grenade or whatever, it always leaves upon impact a large black stain, because a part of the carbon contained in the TNT does not oxidise because there isn't enough strength in it. And to explain it to you as laypersons, just as you have the lead in the pencil, that's the sort of stain it would leave, which mean that the stain was left by the mere impact and not by the explosion which, in fact, took place on the other side of this wall.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should we have our break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I need to, I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a break for ten minutes, after which you will have about 20 minutes. I will consult the court deputy in order to find out the exact time which is remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have, please, a photograph of both walls one by one -- one next to the other. That's 1D022110 -- 1D02210. These are both walls, the photographs of which have been taken from different rooms and they are side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Turkusic, that the length or the distance between the point of impact and the place where this post is on the left photograph is less than the distance on the right-hand side photograph? In other words, in relation to this wall, that the projectile descend in a -- on an acute angle.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the acute angle. What I can say is that according to what the definition of the acute angle is, it doesn't apply here. We can see that the centre of the damage is different, but the difference is minimal and not telling at all, because on the photograph on the left-hand side the point of impact is the result of the explosive charge of the shell, including the shrapnel; whereas on the photograph on the right, the central place of damage is the result of mechanical impact which could be the result of the plaster hitting it or shrapnel hitting and is not indicative at all. This cannot be predicted in any way statistically or -- and it cannot illustrate anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if the impact was the result of a 90 per cent angle of descent -- of a 90-degree angle of descent, would we have the same picture as we do vertically?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does vertically mean? That the shell fell from above, just as the post is vertically to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, horizontally at a 90-degree angle.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the damage -- the distance between the damage on one side of the wall would be the same compared to the other side of the wall?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are presuming in terms of an ideal material. This is not solid material, because you don't know how a rock will react if you hammer -- hammer it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please -- can Mr. Karadzic repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, when we are dealing with technical issues, you need to slow down further considering the difficulties the interpreters are having. The interpreters couldn't hear you, your question, so could you repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you measure the width of this shaft up there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Twenty-five, 30 -- it might be 25, 30 centimetres. We didn't measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you measure the distance from the point of impact on this side of the wall to the point of impact on the other side of the wall?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What impact are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the distance between the post and the centre of impact on this side and the post and the centre of impact on the other side.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was your first question, and I said that we didn't measure it. The distance might be some 20, 30 centimetres, and it doesn't tell you anything at all. An impact into a nonorganic material such as this one, which is lime or cement, such an impact can cause the wall on the other side to break, and it has nothing to do with the impact on this side. However, these two photographs that you wanted us to look at simultaneously absolutely do show that on the left side, that is to say the photograph showing the wall on the left side, we have strong black TNT stains, and that the explosion took place on this side where the shell first hit; whereas on the other side, we only have the mechanical damage which could have been the result of this explosion, and of course, you can have such damage from hitting it merely with a hammer, let alone with such an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So how did you measure the angle of descent in relation to this wall?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we determined the angle of descent regardless of the damage inflicted on the photograph on the right-hand side. On the left-hand side we can see a photograph where the explosion definitely took place. We can see the wings to the left and to the right. We have the black stains, that is, which shows that the shell did not hit the wall horizontally, because then we would have a semicircle. Rather, the shell descended from the -- up above in a slanting manner, and if you want me to draw it -- sideways. I'm trying to activate the pen. That's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness is preparing to draw, I just want to note for the record that the data in yellow and black has been placed on these two pictures by the Karadzic Defence itself. The witness has not yet confirmed any of the information represented by the figures 1, 2, 3, the letters A or B. He hasn't confirmed any of that. So when this is being reviewed in due course, I simply want to note that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, I haven't followed what meanings they have at all for the moment. But the doctor gave us his observation as to the comparison of the two photos, which is helpful. Yes, Doctor, please carry on. Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm having problems with the technology. The pen cannot be activated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Wait until our usher can assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, I can give you my comments on the yellow markings added by the Defence. The dimensions marked A and B and the markings 2 and 3 are absolutely irrelevant to the traces on the other side of the wall, because I've already reiterated three times that the damage on the other side is the result of the impact on this side. Is it working now? No. [In English] It doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we are suffering technical problems. We can't mark on the map -- on the photo for the moment. We should carry on without marking them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is your interpretation of the different distances between the damage on either side of the wall. So your interpretation is that it is due to the peculiar nature of the material involved; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 10144, page 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this to appear, I will read for you from the expert reports by expert Higgs, who disagreed with you, who said in the event where the shell hit a wall, 3.2 metres from the wall, the azimuth cannot be determined as it can when a shell hits the ground resulting in a crater; that is right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if a projectile hits the ground or any other surface we always speak in terms of the degrees of certainty. We had 170 plus/minus 5 in the case of Markale. So we always have a margin of error even where we have certainty. In this case we have a nonspecific impact of a shell, but the determination of cardinal points cannot be an error, and I'm sure that Mr. Higgs did not make a mistake either. He could have made a mistake by some 20 to 30 degrees but not more than that. In any event, it is always north or north-west but definitely not the eastern side when it comes to this shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But if your error was by 30 degrees, will it not have a bearing on the determination of the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us not speculate about the 30 degrees. Tell me what was Mr. Higgs's determination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you if you agree with what Mr. Higgs said, that if you have a shell impacting a place at a height of 3.2 metres from the ground, it is impossible to determine the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree. I will wait. I cannot agree with the findings by Mr. Higgs as you presented them to me. I should like to see what precisely Mr. Higgs said about the determination of the azimuth on the basis of traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not on the basis of traces but on the basis of the place of impact.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we determined the azimuth based on traces, not based on cardinal points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In what cases can a method based on traces be applied when you have an impact on a wall. There you have the analysis by Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the passage you're looking at? The last one in the event where a shell hit a wall 3.2 metres from the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The azimuth cannot be precisely calculated as it can in the case when a projectile makes the usual crater on the ground. I don't know if the translation is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can notice the gasping of the interpreters. This is not an argument. That's the issue asked and answered several times. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yeah. I was going to point out, Mr. President, that Mr. Karadzic has put on the screen what appears to be a translation in B/C/S of Mr. Higgs's report. I request him to give us the precise page and passage in the English language so that we can follow what he's putting to the witness and also so that Your Honours can follow what he's putting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English; right? Mr. Karadzic, I don't know that at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He said 65 ter 10144, page 25. What is this? I see the English version, and we can locate the ... Please carry on, Mr. Karadzic. That has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me just say that on this page Mr. Higgs indicates that the UN team did not agree with your finding.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It turns out that it's my interpretation and that I agree with it. I absolutely disagree in this specific case. It's impossible to determine with respect to both certainty the angle of descent, because it's a very specific geometry of the scene, but the azimuth, which tells us left or right relative to cardinal directions, enables us to determine the direction of fire perhaps a little less precisely than in the case of a shell landing on the ground. That's why I believe the Presiding Judge asked for the English version. Maybe something was lost in the nuances of translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D02205. 1D02205.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the paragraph above this, Mr. Higgs says after it was -- after this, it says it is absolutely possible to determine that the shell came from the west, and Mr. Higgs speaks of an angle of 320 degrees. So we were not wrong, Mr. Karadzic, whereas you were trying to say that we made a lot of mistakes and that we determined everything inaccurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says that line 4 determines pure west, and that's what he says, whereas you said north, Nedzarici. Now, look at this picture.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. What I see on the monitor, can you zoom in a bit. It says: "After the direction west was confirmed," and that means direction west generally, "they used again the traces of explosion and dispersion on the ground and based on them calculated that the shell was fired from a direction which closes the angle of 320 degrees." So west was just determined as a direction. It was oriented.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D02205.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This, Mr. Turkusic, is your sketch related to the orientation on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, he didn't say it was his sketch. A sketch by the CSB team.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant their sketch, their sketch from the investigative material that was decisive for the finding. So this is part of the investigative material.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which angle was definitively determined by Mr. Higgs? Why are you avoiding to tell me that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs commented on your findings and those of the UN, and he disagreed.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did the UN say? Which angle?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't have that finding now, but --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you asked me to confirm that we did not generally disagree in our findings. It was matter of precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Doctor, would you just wait for the accused's question and answer that question, please. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: On this map where -- the sketch from the investigative file of the team of which you were a part of, north shows a deviation of 50 degrees.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 320 to 360, 60 degrees would be missing to make it pure north.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now look at this arrow which shows north on your sketch.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not my sketch. I can't confirm anything that was drawn on a map and I have nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But we agreed that this sketch is part of the investigation file and that based on this, the azimuth was determined.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me as a witness who has certain knowledge and has given an oath and stands by this knowledge. The sketch that you are showing me has nothing to do with my previous experience and my knowledge. You cannot lead me to confirm something that I disagree with and I have no knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. How much would you need for your re-examination, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No more than five minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need about five minutes for administrative matters. You have five minutes. Conclude your cross-examination in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we have your sketch in this case file, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here is a sketch superimposed on the map of Dobrinja by your side. I cannot stand by what is drawn here, because I didn't draw it. And all this analysis which you are trying to push through so quickly would require at least an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Doctor, the question was whether there had been a sketch drawn by you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not this one. I've already said that. I remember sketches that show laterally the projection of the place of impact, possible direction of impact in a cross-section, as we call it, not viewed vertically, downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here you made a sketch of the scene and determined the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then there must be a sketch which bears clear traces of my work. You either don't have that sketch or you're not showing it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To conclude this topic, Mr. Turkusic, we don't have any other sketch apart from the two we've shown. On this sketch, which was authoritative for that investigation, we see north deviating by 50 degrees. If you depicted it on a plane, then you would see that the direction of fire was determined incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're showing me a sketch that I did not make, so you cannot impose on me an interpretation of that sketch.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this, because this is a superb example of how wrong things were done at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can tender that when your expert testifies later on, not with this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go briefly to Markale. We cannot deal with other incidents. Can we just see the footage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have two or three minutes. Whether you can finish or not, it's up to you, after having spent -- wasted a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope I can. If I must, I will. 1D2732.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For whatever purpose, we cannot go further than beyond 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this is indeed the tail fin found at Markale 2, on the site of that incident?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks very much like that tail fin, but many tail fins may have this shape. To identify it as accurately as a finger-print, of course I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you confirmed yesterday's from the movie.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we saw it on the film. It was crushed. We also saw a soldier photographing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the tail fin which is here in the courtroom, and you can tell us if it's the same one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow. We have the tail fin?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Exhibit P1454 in this case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for showing us the tail fin, because the erosion, as you call it, and what we see on this picture, and it really indicates some sort of erosive and abrasive action, is absolutely invisible after 15 years. Any expert in artillery will confirm to you that these deformations on the stabiliser, on the tail fin, are absolutely regular, usual, and standard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection. I'm ready to begin my re-examination now. I believe the accused has used up his time. I'm wondering if he's going to tender two documents concerning the Simon Bolivar school incident which were referred to during cross-examination. In any event, I'd like to do just two minutes of re-examination to allow Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it we can go to five past 12.00, Mr. Registrar? Should be no problem. Just conclude in two minutes. What is your last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you believe that's the tail fin, the one?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the axiometric position consistent with the photograph, it is the tail fin. And we could use -- we should use the physical tail fin, not the picture, because the picture distorts the information. These are no traces of erosion. These are typical traces of explosion, of a strong blast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you claim that this deformation is due to the fact that it was run over by a truck.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is soft tin, and its only job is to keep the shell on course during flight. During flight it bears no other pressure and during firing it also bears no pressure from the impact on its surface. That pressure is only parallel to its shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what happened to the damage to the tail fin which -- that we see on the picture? Is it a living creature so it healed? How do you explain the differences between the picture and the tail fin?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a very precise instrument, you could show that the angles on this tail fin and the distance between the little fins are absolutely identical. What you see on the picture is perhaps not an optical illusion but something like that. These stains on the tail fin could look like that on the picture. A picture is never a 100 per cent reflection of what you see in the flesh, in nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that was your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, can I confirm whether Mr. Karadzic intends to tender 65 ter 15053 and 10144. The first is the case file concerning the Simon Bolivar shelling incident -- school shelling incident. The second is the report of Mr. Richard Higgs, dated 21st of December, 2006. He put a fair number of questions to the witness about those. If he doesn't intend to tender them, I'd tender them in order for Your Honours to be able to assess the witness's credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First one -- 65 ter number of the first thing is 151 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is Mr. Higgs's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It is a report of the 21st December 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which hasn't been tendered yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It has not yet been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence tenders it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then they will be admitted as Defence exhibits. We will give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits D881 and D882, respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, I just want to ask you really one question about one issue. Yesterday you were asked a question by the accused dealing with the issue of repeated shellings. And your answer, which was yesterday's transcript at page 93, reads as follows, I'm going to read a few lines to you: "A. There were several such incidents at funerals when the dead were being buried. One shell would fall. When people are trying to deal with those wounded, then another one would fall in the same place. "Q. Please tell the Trial Chamber when --" sorry, "where and when that happened. "A. In few of the fact that it's been 15 years now, I cannot say that on the basis of memory only. If you insist on that, it is very easy to come by this information." That ends the extract. I'd now like to see if I can refresh your memory with a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I ask -- we're going to play a video with the number -- 65 ter number 40349B, which is an extract of the video 65 ter 40349.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I request that the sound be turned down for the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: "Journalist: When they arrived they were told that Vedrana had already been buried half an hour early because the graveyard was being shelled by the Serbs. That was bad enough but it got much worse. More shells started falling. One landed as the boys and girls from Vedrana's Children's Home arrived with their flowers. As quickly as they could, they dropped them on the graves of Vedrana and the baby boy the sniper also murdered. It was time to go. As the family was leaving. The gunners found their range."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, does that refresh your memory at all on the point you were making?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long time ago I saw this film. If this is not terror against civilians, what is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Mr. Gaynor tell us who filmed this, which TV crew, which broadcasting company, and when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for you. It's -- you can raise it later on. Not at this time. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That ends the re-examination. I tender that video as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has it not been admitted yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It has not yet been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you can answer the question. Can you clarify who filmed?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It was filmed by the BBC and the journalist is Jeremy Bowen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1933, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And also you can tell us later on when it was filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I will do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
